limits_scope: CUDA proof phases. Independent CPU audits, native application/restart and cache-retirement checks ran separately in 3 GiB, four-thread, zero-swap services. Build memory events are recorded separately and are not covered by the zero-event runtime claim.
preserved_failures: qualification-01 rejected coordinator storage before GPU worker launch; zero recursive proofs from that attempt.
qualification-02 combined CLI/library test build reached the 3 GiB build cap and was OOM-killed. The CLI-only rebuild succeeded at the same cap; the full library test build remains unqualified.

Two qualification-02 recovery tests correctly rejected undersized fixture shared reservations. Fixtures now repartition their existing 2 GiB coordinator budget and the added negative regression preserves rejection.

The local prefix-retirement wrapper omitted the pins argument and raised TypeError before cache advice. The corrected wrapper reused the retained pinned inventory after rechecking that all consumers had exited; no proofs were regenerated.
limitations: Every phase has a separate workflow clock. No single 600-second full-block workflow or timing-approved pool is qualified.
Proof observations exclude fresh wallet generation, separate CPU audits and durable native application. They do not establish transactions per hour.
Recovery and multi-candidate pool storage admission retain conservative independent-wallet accounting; the fresh overlap credit does not qualify those 128-input workflows.
File cache advice preserves public artifact bytes. Physical cache release was not measured and no proof or timing authority was granted.
No matched CUDA/OpenCL speed comparison, sustained delivery, power-loss recovery, multi-GPU result or V100 execution is established.
